chapter: Entertainers, Creole Serenaders and La Vida
title: Three big New Orleans bands and playing with Sidney Desvigne and Nelson
summary: He names the big bands (Celestin, Desvigne, Sonny South, Piron) and substitutes with Desvigne and Big Eye Nelson in the 1940s.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well the Celestan band had a lot of guys in it then or was it a small band?
No, Celestan was all, I can tell you at that time there were three big bands, Celestan, Sidney Desbenes, Sonny South, Pierron, all the guys from 10 to 11 there. Yeah, yeah.
Did you ever play with, we talked to all of the losers in the last week or so, Peter Lacazze, did you ever play with him?
No, I don't remember playing with him. But all the regular guys, Nelson, the trombone player, George Nelson. That's his brother, huh?

George Nelson. George Nelson, that's a trombone player. Oh. Lewis Nelson, I think you know about Lewis. Yeah, Lewis Nelson. Lewis Nelson, yeah. Well I worked with him when he was in Sidney's band. You were with Sidney too? You played with Sidney too? Yeah, Substitute's like, you know. Yeah, I worked with him. Talking about Nelson, didn't you play with Big Al Lou Nelson too? Yeah, Big Al Lou I played with Sidney too. When did that happen? That was later on, huh? Well that was around in the forties. Yeah.
I think that was after I came up to the service, I believe in the forties, something like that.
Yeah, it would have been after the service, but it's only a picture in a book.
Yeah. Go back to when, before you went into the service, you know, and I played with Sidney's band.
